newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar to third record close in week.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar to third record close in week.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended early sharp gains to close at a record high on Friday.
Dealers and analysts said the bulls kept charging on the back of a record close on Wall Street and due to favorable fund flows and technical breakouts that had bolstered the bourse all week.
"The Dow definitively had a great impact, and the market is still firm and very positive," a desk trader.
Final closing prices showed the blue chip IPC share index was up 41.85 points on the day, or 1.00 percent, to a new trading and closing record of 4,160.85.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile soared 130.49 points to chalk up an all-time closing high of 7,435.78.
For Felix Boni, research director at ING-Barings, the bourse had upside momentum from breaking through technical barriers earlier in the week and on foreign fund flows.
"The bolsa had been an underperformer relative to Latin America," Boni said.

Boni said the bourse also appeared to be discounting any possible adverse effects of near-term hurdles such as the July 2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates, and Mexican mid-term elections on July 6.
Trading volume, although swollen by some 12 million shares in cross trades, was nonetheless brisk at 142.9 million shares, dealers said.
Dealers said Telmex, which accounted for some 16 percent of all shares traded, drove the market most. The telecom gained 30 centavos to a record close in peso terms of 18.80.
Telmex ADRs climbed 3/4 on Wall Street to 47, a level not seen since the December 1994 peso devaluation crisis. In February 1994, Telmex ADRs traded at more than 74.
Financial firm Bancomer also gained sharply in heavy trade to stand near the top on the leading gainers' list

"Financial stocks had lagged the market, and their second quarter reports should benefit from the downward trend in interest rates and inflation," said Francisco Blanco, research head at the Arka brokerage.
Bancomer's A class shares gained 15 centavos to 1.93 pesos, while the more commonly traded B class ended up 17 centavos at 3.50 pesos.
Dealers noted that financial firm Banacci also gained in healthy volume, climbing 48 centavos to 19.36 pesos.
Bancomer and Banacci are Mexico's two largest brokerage houses.

Retail stock Cifra was one blue chip that notably bucked the rally, closing down 60 centavos to 13.00 pesos on what traders said was a lukewarm market reaction to the terms of merger agreement with Wal-Mart Stores Inc.
Dealers also drew attention to sharp gains by construction firms Empresas ICA and Grupo Tribasa, on expectations a government rescue plan would be forthcoming for troubled highway concessions.
ICA ended up 9.40 pesos to 123.00 pesos, while Tribasa gained 2.00 pesos to 21.00 pesos.
On the broad market, of 117 stocks that changed hands, gainers outpaced sliders by 56 to 42.
Looking ahead to next week, analysts said the bourse still had upside potential, but said strong U.S. producer prices data on June 13 could trip up the market if U.S. long bond yields gained.
(( -- Martin Roberts, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-7907))
